title: MORIAH WIND SYSTEM (MWS)
description: Previously posted under Notice ID N68335-27-Q-0536. This is a revision to change the Notice ID N68335-27-RFI-0536. THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ONLY. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued pursuant to FAR 15.201(e). This RFI is for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation or promise to issue a solicitation in the future. It is a Market Research tool being used to identify potential technologies and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWC-AD) Lakehurst is seeking to continue the production of the U.S. Fleet wind systems for program management, production, systems engineering, logistics support and acceptance for the Moriah Wind System (MWS). The MWS program produces multiple configurations and variants of the MWS and associated components. A description of the Moriah Wind System follows: MWS provides digital wind speed and direction information, including crosswind and headwind, that supports decision making for air operations, combat, navigation, tactical planning and firefighting. The MWS replaces legacy Type F Wind Measuring and Indicating and Digital Wind Systems (DWS), providing a single wind measuring system, consistent across all ship classes, Land Based Test Site, and shore stations. MWS consists of the following main parts: Ultrasonic Wind Sensor Unit (WSU) with non-moving parts Wind Processor unit (WPU) consisting of dual redundant processors capable of interfacing with legacy wind and ship systems and Shipboard Local Area Networks (LANs) High-End Display (HED) with full range of available wind information and ship speed/ course data, including the display of Aircraft Recovery Bulletins (ARBs), Launch and Recovery Envelopes (LREs) and Final Course data. The HED is hardwired to one of the WSUs in a safety critical configuration to enable the display of wind data when the WPU or another connecting network is not functioning. HED fits inside an envelope no larger than11.50� high by 18.00� wide by 9.53� deep. This does not include maintenance access, connector access or environmental excursions. HED must be NVD compatible. Low-End Display (LED) with basic wind information and ship speed/course data. LED fits inside an envelope no larger than 7.36� high by 11.10� wide by 6.06� deep. This does not include maintenance access, connector access or environmental excursions. LED must be NVD compatible. The Air Temperature and Humidity Sensor (ATHU) is an accurate self-contained instrument for measuring external air temperature and humidity. The sensor electronics are enclosed in ruggedized stainless-steel housing. The Air Pressure Unit (APU) is an accurate self-contained instrument for measuring external air pressure. The sensor element and all associated electronics to produce a unidirectional serial data interface are housed in a cast aluminum box. The WSUs, HEDs and LEDs are uniform across ship classes, land-based test sites, and shore stations, with the quantity of each item dependent upon ship class/shore location. Every MWS has one WPU with dual-redundant processors, which will differ depending upon ship class and shore station either of which can individually perform all the functions necessary to keep MWS running. The sub-processors communicate with each other directly and periodically to determine functional status and to allow changes in control when a failure is detected. MWS accesses unclassified data only. There is a degree of system-to-system information exchange in MWS. Neither MWS nor its components are connected to the Global Information Grid (GIG). MWS data is output from its WPU in several ways: 1) synchro interfaces to provide wind information to legacy systems (SLQ-32, SPN-46, Integrated Launch and Recovery Television System (ILARTS), and Arresting Gear Crosscheck System); 2) serial and network interfaces for output of wind, navigational and system information to displays; and 3) network interfaces to communicate wind information to other ship systems and MWS displays. Currently, MWS will communicate over Aviation Data Management and Control System (ADMACS) on CVNs, through Digital Multiplex System (DMS) on DDGs and on a MWS controlled network on all other ship classes. Wind data is transmitted in the standard message format and protocol (SMF&P) data format and the National Marine Electronics Association (NMEA) data format. MWS receives the ARBs it displays through ADMACS via Network File System (NFS). MWS displays LREs that are programmed into the HEDs. In order to display ship�s speed and direction, calculate true wind speed and direction, as well as pitch and roll, MWS receives a data packet from Navigation Sensor System Interface (NAVSSI), which contains a host of navigational data, including ship�s positional information. MWS does not use any of this other information, although it must read the entire NAVSSI data packet prior to extracting the data required. The information in this packet is not sensitive unless the information is transmitted off the ship. However, MWS has no mechanism for transmitting data off the ship, nor any requirement to do so. MWS uses strictly defined data types for transmission into and out of the system. This information is limited to either NMEA ASCII strings using checksums to determine data integrity, structured binary data format using checksums to determine data integrity, proprietary DMS Light Internet Protocol (DLIP), and analog synchro resolver output to other ship systems. The data items themselves are confined to information from known systems (as defined in the relevant Interface Requirements Specifications) or is confined to IP addresses and ports specified in the Interface Design Documents (IDD) and the network architecture (ADMACS, DMS or other ship network). The components contain no TELNET or File Transfer Protocol (FTP) capability. Configuration is done via a manual procedure where a MWS cyber accredited laptop is attached to the system components using a serial cable (RS-422) and programming is done via contractor supplied software applications. The processor software was written to run under a tailored Linux Operating System with minimal functionality on an Intel/ARM platform. This operating system consists of a Linux kernel that has been built specifically for use in this environment that will aid security. It contains only those device drivers and services that are relevant to this embedded environment. Software design protects system integrity by the fact that unauthorized personnel do not have the ability to modify the software configuration, data or application. MWS is not designed for use or visibility on the internet and there is no access to the internet. MWS uses UDP/IP & TCP/IP for unicast and multicast communication protocols. NAWC-AD Lakehurst is requesting information from industry for the purpose of identifying qualified contractors interested in producing MWS. The objective of this is to continue production of the following MWS parts, which establish the current MWS configuration baseline: P/N Nomenclature P/N 81164/0200.00 Wind Sensor Unit (WSU) P/N 82374-0200-00 Wind Sensor Unit (WSU) P/N 81161/0200.00/E High End Display (HED) P/N 82371-0200-00-E High End Display (HED) P/N 81162/0200.00/E Low End Display (LED) P/N 82372-0200-00-E Low End Display (LED) P/N 81161/0102.00 HED LED GUI KIT P/N 82371-0102-00 HED LED GUI KIT P/N 81163/0102.00 WPU GUI KIT P/N 81163/0200.00W01 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V1 P/N 82373-0200-00W01 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V1 P/N 81163/0200.00W04 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V3 P/N 82373-0200-00W04 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V3 P/N 81163/0200.00W05 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V5 P/N 81163/0200.00W06 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V6 P/N 82373-0200-00W07 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V7 P/N PS753 28 VDC Power Supply P/N 81163/0300.00W04 WPU Sub-Processor Unit (SPU) Fiber-optic P/N 82373-0300-

title: Venture-Class Acquisition of Dedicated and Rideshare (VADR) Launch Services
description: NASA Venture-Class Acquisition of Dedicated and Rideshare (VADR) Launch Services 2026 On-Ramp The NASA Venture-Class Acquisition of Dedicated and Rideshare (VADR) Launch Services Request for Proposal (RFP) was issued on May 27, 2021 and remains open for a period of five years from the effective date through the use of an innovative on-ramp provision found in Section 2.11, Clause 2.11.1. The VADR contract�s ordering period remains valid through five years from date of contract award. Currently, there are 13 eligible providers as part of the Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ). These providers are Arrow Science and Technology, LLC, Astra Space, Inc., Blue Origin, LLC, Firefly Aerospace, Inc., Impulse Space, Inc., L2 Solutions, LLC, Momentus Space, LLC, Northrup Grumman System Corp., Phantom Space Corp., Relativity Space, Inc., Rocket Lab USA, Inc., Space Exploration Technologies, Corp., and United Launch Services, LLC. During the life of the solicitation and at the time established via synopsis, the Government will accept proposals from launch service providers for new IDIQ contracts. At a minimum, launch services proposed under VADR require the below: 1. Launch site agreements for at least one launch site to be used in support of task orders awarded under this contract. 2. Evidence of at least one of the following: Launch attempt (intentional ignition) of common launch vehicle configuration being proposed including, but not limited to, the outcome of the launch attempt Successful launch reaching an altitude of 100km or greater (can include any launch vehicle in the Offeror�s fleet) Development tests demonstrating at least 50% of the flight thrust at the complete full-scale single engine assembly level for all core stage engines of the common launch vehicle configuration being proposed. 3. If Offeror is proposing to use a launch vehicle provided by another company e.g., broker services, transfer vehicle, agreements will be required for each proposed vehicle. Original RFP link: https://sam.gov/opp/587b4fae322942b292baccda3098ae13/view (copy and paste into browser) The anticipated RFP will be restricted to domestic sources as described below: DOMESTIC SOURCE CRITERIA In addition to the certification regarding United States commercial provider of space transportation services (Public Law 105?303, Title II, Section 201), the Contractor shall continue to comply with domestic source criteria established below and with United States National Space Transportation Policy, dated November 21, 2013. Failure to comply with the criteria may be grounds for �Termination for Cause� in accordance with FAR 52.212?4(m). Participation in this procurement is restricted to prime Contractors from the United States launch vehicle/services industry. �United States industry� means any corporation, partnership, joint venture, association, or other entity which is organized or existing under the laws of the United States or any State, and whose controlling interest is held by United States citizens. �Launch services� means all services required in the performance of this contract, excluding those necessary to produce or manufacture launch vehicles, its components and other equipment and facilities required in the performance of the contract. �Controlling interest� means ownership of an amount of equity in such entity sufficient to direct management or to void transactions entered into by management. Ownership of at least fifty?one (51) percent of the equity creates a rebuttable presumption that such interest is controlling; however, the ultimate determination as to whether the interest is controlling resides with NASA. The Contractor shall provide in the performance of this contract launch vehicles that are domestic end products. The launch vehicle shall be a domestic end product only if the cost of its components, mined, produced or manufactured in the United States exceeds 50 percent of the cost of all its components. The cost of each component includes transportation costs to the place of incorporation into the launch vehicle and any applicable duty (whether or not a duty?free entry certificate is issued). �Components,� as used in this contract clause, means those materials and supplies directly incorporated into the end product. The Contractor shall provide, in the performance of this contract, domestic launch services. Launch services shall be considered to be domestic if the cost for launch services performed by United States industry sources exceeds 50 percent of the cost of the total required launch services. It is requested that any interested party notify NASA of intent to submit a proposal during this on-ramp period as well as a description of the launch vehicle configuration(s) you intend to propose and current flight manifest. If no viable responses are received, NASA will not conduct a 2026 VADR On-Ramp. An ombudsman has been appointed in accordance with NFS 1852.215-84.

title: E-6B Mobile Sustainment and Support System (MSASS)
description: The Department of the Navy, Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), Airborne Strategic Command, Control and Communications Program Office (PMA-271), intends to award a Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) delivery order under Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) N0001924G0017 to Rockwell Collins Inc., doing business as Collins Aerospace Government Systems (CAGE 13499), for non-recurring engineering to develop and design a Mobile Sustainment and Support System (MSASS) for the E-6B aircraft. The MSASS will function to collect and process communication data for the App Servers in the various Command Management Lan (CML) enclaves. This procurement will additionally include the manufacture and delivery of verification and validation MSASS units to support testing. This action is anticipated to be greater than SAT. This action is not subject to the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement (WTO GPA) and/or a Free Trade Agreement (FTA). This action is not anticipated to be awarded as a construction contract to a small business. This action does not require qualification requirements to be eligible for award. BOA N0001919G0031 was awarded sole source to Collins Aerospace under the authority of 10 U.S.C 3204(a)(1) as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 6.302-1 prior to the Department of War implementation of the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul Part 6 (effective 01 February 2026). Collins Aerospace owns the technical interface documents and the drivers required to meet the backward compatibility requirements to ensure boot up and connections with the stationary SASS and fielded systems on the E-6B aircraft. The Government does not have the technical data rights to the required data sufficient to support a competition. As the OEM of the stationary SASS, Collins is the only contractor with the required expertise to design the MSASS and integrate the systems. Therefore an award to any other source would result in unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency�s requirement since any other source would have to start with a ground up design for MSASS, which would take approximately five (5) years to design, qualify, and integrate into the E-6B. Any technical data associated with this action can be obtained through Collins Aerospace. This action will not be a small business set aside. The NAVAIR Office of Small Business Programs concurs with this set-aside determination. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS, However, all responsible sources may submit a quotation, bid, or proposal, as appropriate, which will be considered by the agency within 15 days after the publication date of this synopsis. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Responses shall be made in writing by e-mail to the attention of Victoria Farrell (victoria.b.farrell2.civ@us.navy.mil) and Lisa Troccoli (lisa.j.troccoli.civ@us.navy.mil). title: Enhanced Mobile Satellite Services (EMSS) Equipment, Provisioning and Customer Care Help Desk Support
description: The United States Space Force (USSF) provides United States Government (USG) and other sponsored customers with satellite communication services through a dedicated, government-controlled gateway. The secure gateway communicates with the contracted commercial Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellation, and traffic processed through the secure gateway may be routed through secure government networks, public telephone networks, or other third-party networks. The program provides cradle-to-grave services and support to its customers, including baseline network airtime access, sale and provisioning of authorized devices, 24/7/365 dedicated help-desk support, enhanced Government capabilities such as encrypted communications, comprehensive operation and maintenance of the secure gateway, and other services. The objective of this possible follow-on effort is to deliver provisioning support and 24/7/365 dedicated help desk support to all authorized EMSS customers, including the Department of War (DoW), Federal Government, State and Local Government, approved foreign and allied governments, and other sponsored customers. The contractor may be required to provide EMSS Service Management services including Telecommunications Service Order (TSO) order management, warranty support, inventory management, supply chain functions, sub-contract management, provisioning activities, gateway liaison services, Return Material Authorization support, reporting, and program management. The scope includes provisioning, invoicing, record management, and customer care services for users who access the commercial satellite constellation through the secure gateway. Services include Telephony (Voice), Data Transmission (Circuit and Packet Switched), Short Burst Data messaging, Tactical Push-to-Talk voice and data, Paging and Alerting, Multicast Data Broadcasts, High-Speed Broadband services, Secure Voice, enhancements/evolutions of those services, and additional commercial services introduced during the period of performance and included under separately managed baseline access agreements. The Performance Work Statement (PES) contained in this posting is a secured attachment. To get access please submit a request through SAM.gov, including at a minimium POC name/contact information, vendor/entity name and CAGE code. Only vendors with Active SAM Registration will be considered for granted access and the Government reserves the right to deny access as it sees fit. These additional security measures are to comply with SF/SSC PA guidance.

title: C-5 Flap Asymmetry Brake Overhaul
description: Pre-Solicitation, C-5 Flap Asymmetry Brake Overhaul NSN: 1680-01-525-8920 (and 1680-01-164-0384) Part Nos: 5903-105L (4C95003-105L) and 5903-105K (4C95003-105K) The United States Air Force (USAF) has a requirement for depot-level overhaul and configuration upgrade of the C-5 Flap Asymmetry Brake. This critical flight control component is part of the Secondary Flight Control Flap System used on the C-5 Galaxy aircraft. It is designed to stop the flap system when an asymmetrical condition is detected in flight, preventing uneven aerodynamic loads and severe damage to the wings and flap actuation system. The purpose of this requirement is two-fold: Overhaul of the 5903-105L configuration assets. Overhaul and Upgrade of the 5903-105K configurations to the final 5903-105L configuration. This effort will utilize a firm-fixed-price (FFP) Requirements Type Contract. The projected period of performance is five (5) years, consisting of a one (1) year basic period and four (4) individual one-year ordering periods. To be eligible for award, offerors must be pre-approved by the Government's Design Control Activity (C-5 AFLCMC/SPO Engineering) in accordance with the Source Pre-Qualification Requirements (SQS). The USAF anticipates this acquisition will be a Full and Open Competition among qualified sources under the SQS, with the basis of award being Lowest Price/Technically Acceptable (LPTA). The Best Estimated Quantities (BEQ) for each ordering period are outlined below: Overhaul CLIN x001 (P/N 5903-105L) Year / Period BEQ Basic 30 EA Ordering Period I 30 EA Ordering Period II 30 EA Ordering Period III 35 EA Ordering Period IV 35 EA Overhaul & Upgrade CLIN x002 (P/N 5903-105K) Year / Period BEQ Basic 10 EA Ordering Period I 10 EA Ordering Period II 10 EA Ordering Period III 10 EA Ordering Period IV 10 EA (Note: Best Estimated Quantities for No Fault Found (NFF) and Beyond Economical Repair (BER) CLINs are estimated at 1 EA per period.) The formal Request for Proposal (RFP) will be posted to the SAM.gov webpage. NO HARDCOPIES WILL BE PROVIDED. All responsible sources qualified under the SQS (or currently seeking qualification) may submit a proposal, which shall be considered by the agency. Offerors are encouraged to register on the site to receive notifications regarding the solicitation and any amendments/revisions.

title: 30 CES FIRE DEPARTMENT - STRUCTURAL FIRE PUMPER VEHICLE LEASE
description: *This amended Presolicitation Notice is to update interested party due date, description and attached Presolicitation Notice* Regulatory Authority and Acquisition Strategy This notice is published in accordance with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 5.101 and 12.201-1 for acquisitions at or below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT), as supplemented by Department of War (DoW) guidance, including DFARS Deviation 2026-O0003 and 2026-O0028. Please note the following: This is a Presolicitation Notice, NOT a Request for Quotations (RFQ). A solicitation document does not currently exist and will not be posted to the Governmentwide Point of Entry (GPE / SAM.gov) or the PIEE Solicitation Module at this time. Following the conclusion of this mandatory 15-day posting period on 10 December 2026, the Government intends to directly solicit quotations from at least three (3) selected sources capable of meeting the requirement, in accordance with RFO 12.201-1(c)(2). The Government does not intend to award a contract based on this presolicitation notice or to pay for the information solicited herein. This notice is issued solely for informational and planning purposes. Notice Regarding Availability of Funds: Funds are not presently available for this effort. No award will be made until funds are available. The Government reserves the right to cancel this presolicitation or any subsequent solicitation, either before or after the closing date. In the event the Government cancels, the Government has no obligation to reimburse an offeror for any costs. Instructions for Interested Parties Although the Government intends to directly solicit quotes from selected vendors after this notice expires, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency in determining the final list of vendors to solicit. Interested parties wishing to demonstrate their capability to fulfill this requirement must submit the following information via email no later than 02:00 PM Pacific Daylight Time (PDT) on 10 December 2026: Company Name, Address, and Point of Contact (Phone & Email) CAGE Code and UEI Number Business Size Standard and Socioeconomic Status under the applicable NAICS code A brief capability statement (maximum of five (5) pages) demonstrating the ability to provide the NFPA 1900-compliant structural fire pumper requested within 10 calendar days of award, provide current third-party annual pump test certification upon delivery, and meet the 24-hour certified EVT maintenance response and 72-hour replacement/loaner requirements. This statement should include relevant past performance examples if available. Submission and Contact Information: All responses and inquiries must be submitted electronically to the primary point of contact listed below. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted. Primary Point of Contact: Jessica Rowe, Contract Specialist, jessica.rowe.5@spaceforce.mil Chase French, Contracting Officer, chase.french@spaceforce.mil
